faq.q: Why does hard rock make a waterfall?
faq.a: Where a river crosses hard rock lying over soft rock, the soft rock erodes faster. The hard layer is left as a ledge the water pours over.
A plunge pool is the deep pool at the foot of a waterfall, dug out by the force of falling water and the rocks it swirls around.
asks: Why is the water deep under a waterfall?

faq.a: The soft rock under the hard ledge is worn away, the ledge collapses, and the edge of the falls moves upstream. Niagara Falls has moved about 11 kilometres upstream in about 12,000 years.
A gorge is a narrow, steep-sided valley. Below many waterfalls, a gorge is left behind as the falls retreat upstream.
Angel Falls in Venezuela is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall on land, about 979 metres high with a single drop of about 807 metres.

facts: Angel Falls in Venezuela is about 979 metres tall, the world's highest waterfall on land.
Niagara Falls has retreated about 11 kilometres upstream over roughly 12,000 years.
